**Fallback accepts schema-valid examples from model reasoning**

A schema-valid example in `<think>` can be returned when the actual answer is missing or off-schema, contrary to `extractJsonFromText`'s handling of reasoning. Remove reasoning blocks from `rawText` before enumerating fallback candidates.



<details>
<summary>Prompt for LLM</summary>

````text
File libs/llm/structured-output-repair.ts, lines 466-468:

Fallback accepts schema-valid examples from model reasoning

The fallback scans fenced blocks inside `<think>` even though `extractJsonFromText` deliberately excludes reasoning, so a schema-valid example in reasoning is returned when the actual answer is off-schema or missing. Remove reasoning blocks before enumerating fallback candidates so those examples cannot be mistaken for the final answer.
````

</details>

**Fallback rescans whole tail for every unbalanced delimiter (quadratic)**

Each unbalanced delimiter makes `sliceBalancedJson` rescan the entire tail, so a brace-heavy or truncated answer blocks the review call with quadratic work per fence. Advance an integer offset over `rest`, and skip the fallback scan entirely when `rest` exceeds a size guard.



<details>
<summary>Prompt for LLM</summary>

````text
File libs/llm/structured-output-repair.ts, lines 501-511:

Fallback rescans whole tail for every unbalanced delimiter (quadratic)

When `sliceBalancedJson` returns null for the delimiter at `start`, the loop advances one character and re-scans the whole remaining tail, so every unbalanced `{`/`[` in the text after a quoted block costs a full scan — a truncated or brace-heavy answer (the cut-payload class this fallback exists for) turns one `repairAndValidate` call into O(delimiters x tail) work per fence and O(fences x delimiters x tail) overall, blocking the review call, and unlike `salvageJsonText` (SALVAGE_MAX_CHARS) there is no size cap on the input. Advance an integer offset over `rest` instead of re-slicing from each delimiter, and skip the whole fallback scan when `rawText` exceeds a sane size guard.
````

</details>
